map.如何从笔法判断一件作品更接近晋人还是唐人？: How can brushwork tell whether a work is closer to the Jin-dynasty or the Tang-dynasty manner?
map.帖学以墨迹法帖为宗，用笔细腻、风格妍美（二王一脉）；碑学尊碑版石刻，取方峻、生拙: The model-copy school (tie xue) takes inked rubbings of famous calligraphic models as its authority, with delicate brushwork and a graceful beauty (the lineage of the two Wang). The stele school (bei xue) reveres carved stone stelae, taking a square, rugged, epigraphic quality (e.g. Northern Wei epitaphs and cliff inscriptions). From the middle of the Qing dynasty the stele school rose, and its works often look heavy and misty, forming a contrast to the flowing elegance of the model-copy school.
map.晋人（如王羲之）重韵致、用笔灵动使转多、结字欹侧自然；唐人重法度、用笔规范、结字: The Jin masters (e.g. Wang Xizhi) valued rhythmic charm, with lively brushwork, many turning and lifting strokes, and naturally inclined character structures; the Tang masters valued strict rules, regulated brushwork and rigorous, even character structures. A regular script work that emphasises the lift-press and pause-press strokes and a canonical frame is closer to the Tang rules, while a running script with flowing connected strokes and a relaxed natural air is closer to the Jin charm.
map.碑帖收藏者比对某名家（如颜真卿、柳公权）用笔结字，判断拓本或临本的流派归属。: Collectors of stela rubbings compare the brushwork and character structure of a famous master (e.g. Yan Zhenqing, Liu Gongquan) to judge the school of a rubbing or a copy.
map.艺术史教学梳理\"晋韵—唐法—宋意—元明复古\"的演变主线。: Art history teaching traces the main evolutionary thread: the Jin charm, the Tang rules, the Song spirit and the Yuan-Ming revival.
map.：颜真卿（颜体）用笔丰腴雄浑、外拓开张，结字宽博端庄（如《多宝塔》《颜勤礼碑》）: : Yan Zhenqing (the Yan style) uses a full, majestic and outward-expanding brushwork with broad, dignified character structures (as in the Duobao Pagoda and Yan Qinli stelae); Liu Gongquan (the Liu style) uses a lean, hard and taut brushwork drawn inward, with character structures tightened at the centre (as in the Xuanmita Stele). The saying "Yan flesh and Liu bone" refers precisely to this contrast between the fuller and the leaner brushwork, and it distinguishes the two great schools of Tang regular script.
